body.title: Durga Puja in Kolkata: from household worship to a city's festival
body.orientation: How a religious festival celebrated by wealthy households became a public festival shaped by neighbourhoods across Kolkata.

paragraphs.text: Durga Puja in Kolkata is an annual Bengali Hindu festival marking the worship of the goddess Durga.
Household pujas came first: one family has organised a puja at its residence in Barisha since 1610, which may be the oldest in the city.

For a long time the festival was confined to wealthy families. In the early twentieth century, community-organised 'barowari' pujas appeared — the first in 1910 in Bhowanipore — and the festival quickly became a common people's celebration.
The festival's history shows how religious practice, urban neighbourhoods and civic life shape one another. In December 2021 it was inscribed on UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage lists.
The claim about the oldest household puja is hedged in the source itself. Accounts from community organisers, artisans and devotees are not represented in this sample.

followUpQuestions: How did Durga Puja come to be recognised by UNESCO?

evidence.excerpt: Since 1610, the Sabarna Roy Choudhury family has been organizing Durga Puja at their original residence in Barisha, Kolkata. This is probably the oldest Durga Puja festival in Kolkata.

claims.text: Earlier confined to wealthy families, the first barowari (community) puja in Kolkata was organised in 1910 in Bhowanipore.

evidence.excerpt: Earlier, Durga Puja in Kolkata was confined to wealthy families. In 1910, the first Barowari Durga Puja in Kolkata was organized by "Bhowanipore Sanatan Dharmatsahini Sabha" at Balram Basu Ghat Road, Bhowanipore.
